clue.text: One sweeping round every bit of dance floor

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece is wrapped about the other

blocks.note: a broom is the thing that does the sweeping
every bit of something is all of it

explanation.surface: Someone sweeps up every last bit of the dance floor after the night ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One sweeping' is not a description of a dancer gliding round the floor; it names the thing that sweeps.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom is a large hall built for dancing, so the whole space is effectively one big floor for dancers.

blocks.note: first meaning: leave out or pass over
second meaning: a shortened form of skipper, the captain of a side

explanation.surface: A manager decides to drop the team captain from the side for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip is to pass over or leave out, and the same word is a clipped form of skipper, a sports captain.

clue.text: Scots toss them live into vehicles

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside, so these letters sit within the others

blocks.note: cars are road vehicles
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Scotsmen hurl living creatures into cars, an absurd picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossing the caber, a long tree trunk thrown end over end, is a Scottish Highland Games event.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabers are the heavy wooden poles thrown end over end in Highland Games contests in Scotland.

indicators.note: the word says the name is to be found inside the other piece

blocks.note: spots are places or locations
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Les judges certain locations to be perfectly clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In places' reads as 'in some spots', but 'In' is the instruction to put the name inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spotless has no mark or stain at all, which is what being perfectly clean and faultless means.

indicators.note: the words could be something else, inviting their letters to be rearranged into another word

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Being capable and so forth might be all that is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Acceptable means adequate or satisfactory, good enough to pass even if not outstanding.

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the word is altered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Quiet physicians attend closely to their patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctors' reads as a plural noun but works as a verb meaning tampers with.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to give heed with your ears, the same as concentrating on what is said.

clue.text: Support part of body after a stroke

blocks.note: to back someone is to support them
the hand is a part of the body

explanation.surface: Someone needs support for a body part following a medical stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a stroke' suggests an illness, but here it is a shot in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhand is a racket shot played with the back of the hand facing the direction of play, a type of tennis stroke.

clue.text: Summary of archaeological excavation is in French

blocks.note: a dig is an archaeological excavation
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A report on an archaeological dig has been written in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a condensed version of a longer text, a compilation or abridgement of the main points.

blocks.note: surface reading: dining at a restaurant rather than at home
setter's reading: eating literally out of doors, on a blanket in a field

explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' normally means going to a restaurant; the question mark tells you to take 'out' literally as outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is a meal taken in the open air, often packed in a basket and eaten on the grass.

blocks.note: first meaning: a small piece of paper, such as a betting or pay ticket
second meaning: a small mistake

explanation.surface: A mistake might have been made on a ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small strip of paper like a receipt, and also a minor blunder or lapse.

clue.text: Of course it's the last time you'll need a driver!

definitions.text: Of course it's the last time you'll need a driver!

blocks.clueFragment: Of course it's the last time you'll need a driver!
blocks.note: surface reading: someone reassuring a passenger that they won't need a chauffeur again

blocks.clueFragment: Of course it's the last time you'll need a driver!
blocks.note: setter's reading: on a golf course, the final hole is the last where a golfer tees off with the club called a driver

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' sounds like 'certainly', but means 'belonging to a golf course'; a driver is the long-hitting golf club, not a chauffeur.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard golf round has eighteen holes, so the final one is the last tee shot needing that club.

blocks.note: first meaning: climbs aboard a ship, train or plane
second meaning: the theatre

explanation.surface: An actor makes it into the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To board is to go aboard a vehicle, and the boards is an idiom for the theatrical stage and acting profession.

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
creation is the whole created world and everything living in it

explanation.surface: A drama concerning every creature on earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a theatrical piece, but it means leisure activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreation is leisure activity done for enjoyment, which is what play means as a noun.

clue.text: Gas went out and I admitted perspiring

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or askew, so the letters are put into a different order
something admitted is let inside, so the single letter is put within the rest

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: The gas supply failed and someone owns up while dripping with nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweating is giving off moisture through the skin, the plain word for perspiring.

clue.text: Old lady, 100, was replaced by parrots

indicators.note: something replaced is put back differently, so the letters return in another order

blocks.note: an old lady is slang for one's mother, ma
C is the Roman numeral for 100
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A centenarian woman has been supplanted by talking birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old lady' is informal for mother, hence MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaws are large brightly coloured tropical birds belonging to the parrot family.

blocks.note: a machine that works is operating
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Someone runs a dance studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dance studio' reads as one phrase, but 'dance' belongs to the wordplay and 'studio' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A workshop is a room where things are made or practised, similar to an artist's or craftsperson's studio.

blocks.note: US is short for the United States, hence American
an able person is skilled or expert

explanation.surface: A skilled American professional is available to help.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usable is available and fit to be put to use, which is what having it at hand means.

indicators.note: a thing working is being processed or manipulated, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged; the possessive s is not used

explanation.surface: Ted has his holiday entitlement increased now he is employed.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the letters of 'leave' and 'Ted' are used; the apostrophe-s reads as 'is', a link joining fodder to indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevated means lifted up to a higher position, the same as raised as an adjective or past participle.

clue.text: Devotee did move during the performance

indicators.note: to move letters is to shift them around into a fresh arrangement
something happening during an event sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an act is a performance
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dedicated fan dances along while the show is on.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict can mean an enthusiast or fan hooked on a hobby, not only someone dependent on a drug.

clue.text: Looked to have imitated said pair breaking in

indicators.note: said tells us to go by how the word is spoken, not how it is spelt
a burglar breaking in gets inside, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to ape is to imitate
the fruit is pronounced the same as a couple

explanation.surface: A copycat couple seems to have burgled the place.
explanation.walkthrough: The couple is never spelt out: only its spoken sound, a fruit, goes into the word for copied.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeared means seemed, as in 'he looked tired', so the two verbs share a past tense sense.

blocks.note: first meaning: money gained from a sale, as a noun
second meaning: make a lot of money, as a verb

explanation.surface: Someone goes on to tidy the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' looks like a verb, 'goes on', but it is the noun for takings.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is financial gain from a sale, and to clean up is an idiom for making a large financial gain.

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its start, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
a lever is a rigid bar used to prise things

explanation.surface: A newly opened bar at a club proves a stylish venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club bar' looks like a drinking place; bar here is a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and smart both mean quick-witted and intelligent.

clue.text: It's not clear if it is

definitions.text: It's not clear if it is

blocks.clueFragment: It's not clear if it is
blocks.note: surface reading: a vague remark that the matter is uncertain

blocks.clueFragment: It's not clear if it is
blocks.note: setter's reading: when the weather or a liquid is this, it is literally not clear

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like doubt about whether something is true; read it as 'if it is this, it is not clear', describing murky sky or water.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloudy describes a sky full of clouds or a liquid that is murky, opaque and not transparent.

clue.text: Changing rooms, if it's very loud

indicators.note: changing something alters it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting changed in a changing room is noisy business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if it's' does double duty in the surface but its letters all belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortissimo is the Italian musical direction telling performers to play extremely forcefully, at the highest volume.

blocks.note: first meaning: a substance for washing
second meaning: a long-running TV drama serial, of which this is one example

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady comes from the setting of a famous TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: Coronation Street is a long-running British TV soap opera set in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap is a washing product, and a soap opera, shortened to soap, is a TV serial like Coronation Street.

blocks.note: first meaning: an attempt
second meaning: a turn, as in whose go is it

explanation.definitionFit: A shot is an attempt at something, and also someone's turn in a game, both nouns.

clue.text: OK, I'm on about a dressinggown

indicators.note: to turn about is to change round, so the letters are shuffled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to go on stage chatting about a robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is a loose wide-sleeved Japanese robe, and the name is also used for a light wraparound bathrobe.

clue.text: Very little bars for tiny swimmers

blocks.note: a tad is a very small amount
poles are long bars or rods

explanation.surface: Pools offer barely any rails for small children in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Tadpoles are the small aquatic larvae of frogs and toads, which wriggle through ponds with their tails.
